detail:
A 2026 article in Frontiers in Neurology describes how the success of modern migraine therapeutics is forcing a re-evaluation of how preventive trials are designed. The shift began with the American Headache Society's 2024 position statement, which concluded that CGRP-targeting therapies should be considered a first-line option for migraine prevention, alongside traditional oral preventives, without requiring patients to fail older medication classes first.

Because an effective standard of care now exists, the article argues, the blanket justification for placebo-only comparison groups weakens in many preventive-trial settings, and research attention turns to active-comparator designs, long-term safety, and access. For readers, the practical point is narrower: the preventive landscape changed quickly, and which option fits a given person remains a clinical decision.

Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
sourceVideoTitle: A victim of its own progress: why the success of modern therapeutics forces a re-evaluation of placebo-controlled trials in migraine prevention
summary: With CGRP-targeting therapies established as a first-line preventive option in the American Headache Society's 2024 position statement, current research debates how to test the next generation of migraine treatments fairly against effective existing options.
takeaways: cgrp therapies moved to a first-line preventive option in 2024
research now compares new drugs against active treatments
long-term safety, access, and trial design remain open questions
trial results do not change your plan; discuss options with your doctor
title: After CGRP: migraine research's next questions
